title: Permits for a Hotel, Guesthouse and Commercial Villa in Bali | SAFRWAY
seoTitleLiteral: Hotel and Villa Licensing in Bali — OSS, PBG, SLF | SAFRWAY
metaDescriptionLiteral: Checking whether a hotel, guesthouse or rental villa can operate legally: KBLI, land designation, OSS/NIB, PBG/SLF and sector-specific permits.

faq.question: Can any villa be rented out to tourists if there is a lease agreement?
faq.answerMarkdown: There is no universal guarantee. A lease agreement alone does not replace the requirements applicable to the business activity and the property.

faq.question: Does a foreign operator need a PT PMA?
faq.answerMarkdown: It depends on the business structure, whether foreign participation is permitted and the type of activity; this is checked before choosing a company form.

faq.question: Is an NIB enough for a hotel?
faq.answerMarkdown: Not always. Requirements depend on the sector-specific category and the status of the property's documents.

faq.question: Is there a special licence for every villa?
faq.answerMarkdown: The specific set of permits depends on the accommodation model, the property and the operator. We determine the KBLI code and type of activity first, then the documents.

faq.question: Do you check PBG and SLF?
faq.answerMarkdown: Yes. As part of the preliminary assessment, we establish whether these documents exist and whether they correspond to the property. Any need for further action is determined for the specific property.

faq.question: If a villa is already listed on a booking platform, does that mean everything is legal?
faq.answerMarkdown: Not necessarily. Publishing a listing does not prove compliance with OSS requirements, building rules or local regulations.

faq.question: Can you check a location before purchase or rental?
faq.answerMarkdown: Yes. This is one of the most useful stages: establishing restrictions before committing funds.
